name: Step-Up with Barbell
description: The barbell step-up is a unilateral lower body exercise performed with a barbell across the traps, stepping onto a box or bench. The added load of the barbell dramatically increases the difficulty compared to dumbbell step-ups and challenges the quadriceps, glutes, and hip extensors of the working leg. The box height determines the range of motion and muscle emphasis.

execution.starting_position: Unrack the barbell and position it across the upper traps. Stand facing a sturdy box or bench at knee height.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a box height that creates approximately 90 degrees of knee flexion when the foot is on top. Load conservatively.
steps: Step 1: Place the working foot fully on the box, ensuring the entire foot is on the surface.
Step 2: Drive through the working heel to extend the leg and lift the body onto the box.
Step 3: Stand fully upright on the box, bringing the trail foot up to touch the box surface (not pushing off with it).
Step 4: Lower the trail foot back to the floor in a controlled manner and repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the step up, inhale on the controlled descent.
common_mistakes: Pushing off the floor foot, reducing working leg demand
safety_considerations: Ensure the box is completely stable and can safely support the loaded barbell weight
Develop with dumbbell step-ups before using a barbell
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the top of the box. Full descent to both feet on the floor.
coaching_cues: Drive through the heel on the box
